steps.note: an icon drawn with the Pen on a blank white canvas. The white is a real full size bitmap under the shape, so a PNG of this either carries it in every pixel or does not
Export on PNG. Under the pixel size there is now a line saying what the file will weigh, in the same place and the same words the lossy formats use, with Lossless where they name a quality

the background ticked back on, so the white canvas goes into the file. The weight line answers: this is the number the box was hiding, and the drop between this reading and the one before it is the whole point of the change
untick it and the number goes back down. Nothing about the sheet moves except the size, so the eye stays where it was
2x asked for: four times the pixels, so a much bigger file, and the line says how much bigger before anybody saves it. This is the same number the lossy formats have always moved with the scale row
the same sheet on JPEG: the size sits on the same line, under the quality slider that only a lossy format has. Same name, same place, so switching format never moves the number somewhere else

the same two files really written, so the two numbers the sheet showed can be weighed on disk. A flat canvas costs a PNG very little, which is itself worth knowing before you save: leaving it out buys you transparency, not a much smaller file
